chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Exalted is His Praise: 'Then let them fulfill their needful acts.' He said: 'It is what happens from the man who is in his Ihram. So when he enters Makkah, so he would speak with good speech. That would be an expiation for that which was from him.'

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: his state of Ihram (sacred consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.تَفَثُهُمْ: their needful acts / what is necessary for them

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'Then let them fulfill their needful acts' mean in the context of Hajj rituals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) interprets the phrase 'fulfill their needful acts' (or 'cut off their impurities') as a directive for pilgrims to purify themselves through good speech and conduct upon entering Makkah. This interpretation highlights the spiritual dimension of Hajj, where verbal and behavioral rectification serves as expiation (*kaffarah*) for minor sins or shortcomings incurred during the state of Ihram, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner purity alongside ritual observance.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Abu Baseer,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the Words of Allahazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Praise [22:29] Then let them fulfil their needful acts. Heasws said: ‘It is what happens from the man who is in his Ihraam. So when he enters Makkah, so he would speak with the good speech. That would be an expiation for that which was from him’.
en.sarwar: 15. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said the following

about the words of Allah, glorious is whose praise, ‘They should spruce up.’ He (the Imam) said that this is about what one may have had in the state of Ihram. When he enters Makkah, he should speak proper words and this will be considered as expiation for what he has had in the state of Ihram.’”
